question: What makes an external means effective for liberation in the teacher-disciple relation?
premises: An external means by itself is not the cause of liberation.
Teacher and disciple must share the firm recognition 'this is Shiva; I am Shiva.'
inference: External practice gives liberation only when it is grounded in a firm Shiva-identification shared by teacher and disciple.
uncertainties: The compound at the end is compressed; the exact distribution of the recognition between teacher and disciple is interpretive.
plain_english: An external means identified with Shiva is not by itself what gives liberation. Liberation comes when teacher and disciple firmly hold the recognition: this is Shiva; I am indeed Shiva.
